headline: Chilly mornings with possible frost early in the week, then a quiet pattern with only light rain possible late week.
summary:
A low-pressure trough of cold air aloft is moving south, well off the coast, and will be farther away by Tuesday. Western Washington stays on the quiet side. High clouds are streaming in tonight, and the forecast is unchanged from earlier.

The main thing people may notice is the cool mornings. Lows Monday morning should be in the mid 30s around Olympia and south along the I-5 corridor, and in the mid 40s elsewhere. Tuesday morning lows drop a few more degrees, so frost is possible in the south Puget Sound and Chehalis Valley, and also in the Cascades and valleys. Patchy morning fog is possible early in the week, most likely in valleys and other spots that tend to get fog.

Later in the week, a weak system may bring light rain Thursday into Friday. If precipitation does develop, snow levels could fall to around 4,000 to 4,500 feet, so a few light snow flurries are possible at those heights and above. Forecasters do not expect much impactful weather. The coast may also see a larger swell around Thursday, with waves near 10 to 12 feet offshore.

timeline.what: High clouds move in ahead of the departing trough. No changes to the forecast.
Lows in the mid 30s from Olympia south through the I-5 corridor and in the mid 40s elsewhere. Patchy fog is possible, mainly in valleys and fog-prone spots.
Lows fall a few degrees further. Frost is possible in the south Puget Sound, Chehalis Valley, Cascades, and valleys. Patchy fog is still possible.
A flat, mostly west-to-east pattern aloft sets up. Troughing builds over the Gulf of Alaska while a deeper low moves into southern California.
Light rain is possible. If precipitation develops, light snow flurries are possible at about 4,000 to 4,500 feet and higher.
The position of the low becomes less clear, but forecasters do not expect much impactful weather.

confidence: Forecasters appear fairly confident about the quiet, cool start to the week, since the forecast is unchanged. Confidence drops for late week: they say the low's position is less clear by Friday into the weekend. They also hedge on the light rain and snow flurries, which would happen only if precipitation materializes.

glossary.definition: An elongated area of lower pressure in the upper atmosphere, often linked with cooler, unsettled weather. Here, one is moving south and staying well offshore.
A pattern in which the winds high above the ground blow mostly from west to east with few big bends. It usually means fewer sharp weather changes.
Groups of computer forecasts run with slightly different starting conditions. When they agree, forecasters have more confidence.
A trough of low pressure aloft over the Gulf of Alaska, the ocean area north of the Pacific Northwest. Forecasters expect it to build there starting Wednesday.
The elevation above which precipitation falls as snow instead of rain. A snow level of 4,000 to 4,500 feet means flurries are possible only at those heights and above.
Long, regular ocean waves generated by distant storms. They can reach the coast even when local weather is calm.
